system.summary: Graphic-sign simple substitution of English, words divided, a few homophones (d/u share a sign, a/g), single signs for persons (9, n, pound sign), inserted as runs in clear English.
system.notes: Same key in all six letters, 1593 (dated 1592, English year) and 1594, in two hands.

prior_solution.where: G. G. Butler, The Edmondes Papers (Roxburghe Club, 1913), nos. XVIII, XXI, XXII, XXIII and LXVI (pp. 46-59, 148-151), prints five of the six letters (R7770-R7773, R7775) from Stowe 166 with the cipher passages deciphered, apparently in italics with a 'cypher' note. Shown on 2026-09-30 from HathiTrust Research Center page-level word data for mdp.39015083993017 (e.g. all 17 words of the f. 58v passage on p. 56); Butler's wording not seen, because HathiTrust and Google Books block this machine. R7774 (ff. 109-110) is not printed. R. S. Love, Blood and Religion (2001) also quotes the f. 50 and f. 60v passages from the letters as received (PRO uncalendared State Papers). DECODE: Non-decrypted; no decipherment on the leaves; not in Birch 1749 or HMC Salisbury IV; List and Analysis SP Foreign vols 3-5 not seen.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: DECODE login cookie, Claude Code set-up, the problem posed with /goal; said 'continue' after a subagent was blocked.

solution.what: Fetched 24 page images and record metadata for R7770-R7775 from DECODE with the session cookie.
Metadata 'author: Lord Threr?' read as the addressee; BL catalogue identifies Stowe MS 166 as Edmondes's papers.
Searched Birch 1749 (archive.org text) for the passages; Butler 1913 blocked (HathiTrust 403).
f. 50: frequent words taken as the/of/to; then 'difficulties', 'empeachement' on f. 109v fixed most letters.
Subagent read f. 50 in full (marriage of the King's sister, person signs 9 and n); it was blocked by auto mode before the other pages.
Read f. 57, f. 58v, f. 60v, f. 109v, f. 112 from line crops with the key.
Four cipher lines on f. 59 attempted; only fragments.

Print check: Butler, Edmondes Papers (1913) located as HathiTrust full view mdp.39015083993017 (record 002098089), but ssd/pt/full-text search blocked by Cloudflare 403 after one page (curl, PowerShell, WebFetch); Google Books 4sJCAQAAMAAJ captcha, Books API over quota; not on archive.org. List and Analysis of State Papers Foreign 1591-94 in copyright, BHO premium only; not searched.

Butler 1913 retried directly. HathiTrust still blocks this machine: imgsrv answers 'Blocked from HathiTrust' on IP reputation (IPv4 and IPv6), and pt, pt/search, ssd and ls give a Cloudflare challenge. Google Books redirects to its captcha page (not followed); the Books API quota is 0; there is no archive.org copy. Birch 1749 re-grepped in three archive.org texts: his Edmondes narrative jumps from Chartres, 25 Nov 1592 to Sept 1594 and prints none of the six letters.

Butler 1913 checked through the HathiTrust Research Center Extracted Features 2.0 file for mdp.39015083993017 (open per-page OCR word counts, 532 pages; targets/stowe166/butler1913_check.py). Butler's 'Stowe MS. 166, f. ...' source notes and running heads identify R7770 = no. XVIII (Chartres, 19 Jan 1593, pp. 46-48), R7771 = XXI (Tours, 16 Feb 1593, pp. 51-54), R7772 = XXII (Tours, 3 Mar 1593, pp. 54-57), R7773 = XXIII (Blois, 16 Mar 1593, pp. 57-59) and R7775 = LXVI (Laon, 23 Jul 1594, pp. 148-151); R7774 (ff. 109-110) is not printed. The words of each passage read here stand on its Butler page: f. 58v 17/17 on p. 56 (no other page above 5/17), f. 50 10/12, f. 57 7/7, f. 112 5/5, and f. 60v 'vendible' split by the italic OCR. Each page has a 'cypher' note. So Butler printed the cipher passages deciphered, including f. 59 (candidate words on p. 56). The data has no word order, so his wording is unseen.

archive.org full-text search. R. S. Love, Blood and Religion (2001), quotes the f. 50 passage ('great hope, that he [i.e., Montpensier] will render himself of the Religion', cited as Edmondes to Burghley, 19 Jan and 3 Mar 1593, PRO uncalendared State Papers) and 'faith is not vendible' (f. 60v), from the letters as received; his bibliography does not list Butler. HMC Salisbury IV (1892), pp. 559-560, prints a different Edmondes letter from the camp before Laon (9 Jul 1594) with its cipher undeciphered, and none of ours. Stevenson's Unton Correspondence (1847) prints Unton's 1591 cypher, a different key.

Dating checked. Edmondes wrote the English year, which began on 25 March. Butler's running heads put ff. 50-61 in Jan-Mar 1593, and the 1895 BL Stowe catalogue starts the volume on 18 June 1592, with f. 27 (26 Sept 1592) promising the Unton cypher. So 'Tours, 3 Mar 1592' and 'Blois, 16 Mar 1592' are 1593 in modern reckoning, and the document years were corrected from 1592 to 1593.

R7772 images re-fetched from DECODE with the account cookie (IMG_R7772_I35130_P1-P4, 6484x8820; img/ git-ignored); the four cipher lines are at the head of f. 59 (image P3), partly under the turned-in edge of f. 60 in the photograph but legible
f. 59 four cipher lines transcribed sign by sign (f59_r7772.txt, 126 signs)

Decoded with the Stowe 166 key: 'and by consequence popis[h]lie nourished pretending so to appertaine to the place of the constable to haue the gouer[n]ment of the younge heire of the crowne', continuing the f. 58v passage on Montmorency and the young Prince of Condé; one new sign, a vertical stroke = q (consequence)

Compared with Butler 1913 p. 56 (seq 104) by the HathiTrust Extracted Features word bag: all 20 distinct words of the decipherment are on the page in Butler's modern spelling (popishly, nourished, pretending, appertain, constable, government, young, heir, crown); the next best page has 10. Page text still blocked

Known keys checked for the person signs: Tomokiyo's Elizabethan cipher tables (elizabeth.htm copy) have no Edmondes table; Unton's 1591 cypher (Stevenson 1847 p. 14) is a different system; the DECODE harvest has no Edmondes key record
R7774 and R7775 images re-fetched from DECODE (cookie); f. 109v and f. 112 cipher lines re-read

R7774 lines 1-2 (missing from the earlier reading): '[9]: of whome especiallie [o] hath made choise...'; the old '[?]' is the same sign o, a person sign (the King? by context); R7775 lacuna read 'carryinge' (r+y ligature)
reading.txt + measure.py: 1023/1035 cipher signs read = 98.8% (11 person code signs, 1 unexplained sign)
Person signs: HMC Salisbury IV and Birch 1749 (searched 30 Sept) print no decipherment naming them; CSP Foreign/List and Analysis 1592-94 not online; Butler pages blocked

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 126 tokens, 19 types, en-1640s order 4: reading -2.279 per letter; random keys -6.414 (z 5.7); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -3.372 (mean -3.552, z 7.6); annealer on the real text -2.443. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -1.866; polyphony 0.048; 0 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.443

outcome.method_basis: The simple substitution was broken from frequent cipher words guessed as 'the', 'of', 'to' and then 'difficulties', 'empeachement' on f. 109v, with no printed or glossed plaintext in hand. Butler 1913, which prints five of the six letters deciphered, was found on 2026-09-30, after the reading, so this is an independent re-solution of a published decipherment (see conditions.prior_solution).
